runs.command: uv run python -m evals_audio --suite tempo --dataset ballroom --limit 50 --seed 1
runs.selection: 50 of 698 usable tracks drawn with numpy default_rng(1)

dataset.name: ballroom
dataset.title: Ballroom (ISMIR 2004 tempo induction contest)
dataset.annotationLicence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/), per mirdata 1.0.0 (ballroom.LICENSE_INFO); not stated by the dataset: the contest page states no licence
dataset.audioRights: commercial excerpts (BallroomDancers.com, credited on the contest page); no licence is stated for the audio. Fetched into the local data directory for evaluation only and never redistributed: the repository holds no audio and no audio file names.
credits: Gouyon, F., Klapuri, A., Dixon, S., Alonso, M., Tzanetakis, G., Uhle, C., Cano, P. (2006). An experimental comparison of audio tempo induction algorithms. IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing 14(5), 1832-1844. doi:10.1109/TSA.2005.858509
dataset.referenceNote: the contest's ground-truth tempo (one value per excerpt)
notes: 698 excerpts of about 30 s from BallroomDancers.com, eight dance styles, so the 30 s window covers nearly all of each excerpt.
Published Ballroom figures use all 698 excerpts; a sample of n clips is only comparable within its interval.

Ballroom's track ids are its file names (album names included), so the results use the first 10 hex digits of a SHA-256 of the dataset name and the id; `uv run python -m evals_audio --lookup ID --dataset ballroom` maps one back from the local index.

estimatorNotes: beat-this's checkpoint was trained on every dataset its authors used except GTZAN, Ballroom included (CPJKU/beat_this_annotations lists ballroom; the authors warn that results on training data are unfairly good). Its Ballroom numbers are on its own training data: they are shown, marked, but they say nothing about new music and are kept out of the bake-off conclusion (its pair tables on this dataset are not printed).
estimatorCredits: Foscarin, F., Schlüter, J., Widmer, G. (2024). Beat this! Accurate beat tracking without DBN postprocessing. Proc. ISMIR 2024. arXiv:2407.21658. https://github.com/CPJKU/beat_this: the code and the published model weights (checkpoint final0, from the authors' cloud space) are under the MIT licence

runs.command: uv run python -m evals_audio --suite tempo --dataset giantsteps-tempo --limit 200 --seed 1
runs.selection: 200 of 661 usable tracks drawn with numpy default_rng(1)

dataset.name: giantsteps-tempo
dataset.title: GiantSteps Tempo
dataset.annotationLicence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/), per mirdata 1.0.0 (giantsteps_tempo.LICENSE_INFO); not stated by the dataset: the annotation repository has no licence
dataset.audioRights: commercial excerpts (Beatport two-minute previews); no licence is stated for the audio. Fetched into the local data directory for evaluation only and never redistributed: the repository holds no audio and no audio file names.
credits: Knees, P., Faraldo, Á., Herrera, P., Vogl, R., Böck, S., Hörschläger, F., Le Goff, M. (2015). Two data sets for tempo estimation and key detection in electronic dance music annotated from user corrections. Proc. ISMIR 2015, 364-370. doi:10.5281/zenodo.1414996
Schreiber, H., Müller, M. (2018). A crowdsourced experiment for tempo estimation of electronic dance music. Proc. ISMIR 2018. doi:10.5281/zenodo.1492437 (the v2 annotations used here)
dataset.referenceNote: annotations_v2 (Schreiber & Müller 2018): of the tempi the crowd tapped, the one with the highest share
notes: 664 two-minute Beatport previews of electronic dance music.
mirdata does not download this audio; the harness uses the locations in the dataset's download script and checks each file's MD5.

Published GiantSteps Tempo figures are computed on the whole two-minute previews, mostly against the v1 labels; here one 30 s window per preview is scored against v2, and the window can fall on an intro, a breakdown or the fade. Not comparable.

estimatorCredits: Foscarin, F., Schlüter, J., Widmer, G. (2024). Beat this! Accurate beat tracking without DBN postprocessing. Proc. ISMIR 2024. arXiv:2407.21658. https://github.com/CPJKU/beat_this: the code and the published model weights (checkpoint final0, from the authors' cloud space) are under the MIT licence

dataset.name: giantsteps-key
dataset.title: GiantSteps Key, as GiantSteps+ (Faraldo 2017 revision)
dataset.annotationLicence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/), stated in the Zenodo record (10.5281/zenodo.1095691); mirdata 1.0.0 agrees
dataset.audioRights: commercial excerpts (Beatport two-minute previews; the record says the audio belongs to Beatport); no licence is stated for the audio. Fetched into the local data directory for evaluation only and never redistributed: the repository holds no audio and no audio file names.
credits: Faraldo, Á. (2017). GiantSteps+ EDM Key Dataset. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.1095691
Faraldo, Á. (2017). Tonality Estimation in Electronic Dance Music: A Computational and Musically Informed Examination. PhD thesis, Universitat Pompeu Fabra, Barcelona

Knees, P., Faraldo, Á., Herrera, P., Vogl, R., Böck, S., Hörschläger, F., Le Goff, M. (2015). Two data sets for tempo estimation and key detection in electronic dance music annotated from user corrections. Proc. ISMIR 2015, 364-370. doi:10.5281/zenodo.1414996 (the original GiantSteps Key dataset)
The record's description asks for 10.5281/zenodo.1101082, but that DOI resolves to a different record (the Beatport EDM Key Dataset, 1,486 excerpts); the record used here is cited above
dataset.referenceNote: the GiantSteps+ single-key label (keys_gs+), tonic and major/minor
notes: 600 two-minute Beatport previews of electronic dance music. mirdata's giantsteps_key loader is the GiantSteps+ revision of the original GiantSteps Key labels, with the audio published on Zenodo.

Labels with two keys ('E major | E minor'), 'other' modes, 'X' or a misspelt tonic are not scored and are counted as unusable; modal labels keep their major/minor word ('F minor dorian' is scored as F minor).

Published GiantSteps Key figures are computed on the whole two-minute previews, mostly against the original 2015 labels; here one 30 s window per preview is scored against GiantSteps+ with the ambiguous labels left out. Not comparable.

runs.trainedOnNote: A lower bound: the golden songs were matched by title and artist against the Harmonix Set's metadata. The track names of the other training sets (8-folds.split in CPJKU/beat_this_annotations) hold no golden song where they name one (ASAP, Beatles, Candombe, Filosax, Groove MIDI, GuitarSet, HJDB, JAAH, RWC, SIMAC), but Hainsworth, SMC and part of SIMAC give numbers only and TapCorrect gives YouTube ids, so a golden song there would not be found. Harmonix also has a remix edit of "Alors on danse" (Stromae's production, another recording) and Lionel Richie's 2012 duet of "Hello"; neither is counted.
estimatorCredits: Foscarin, F., Schlüter, J., Widmer, G. (2024). Beat this! Accurate beat tracking without DBN postprocessing. Proc. ISMIR 2024. arXiv:2407.21658. https://github.com/CPJKU/beat_this: the code and the published model weights (checkpoint final0, from the authors' cloud space) are under the MIT licence

Nieto, O., McCallum, M., Davies, M., Robertson, A., Stark, A., Egozy, E. (2019). The Harmonix Set: beats, downbeats, and functional segment annotations of Western popular music. Proc. ISMIR 2019. https://github.com/urinieto/harmonixset (MIT); its metadata was used to find golden songs in beat-this's training data
